sentences.text: Ptyctodus was an extinct fish belonging to the class Placodermi, a group of armored fishes, that lived during the late Devonian period.
This creature closely resembles modern chimaeras, or Holocephali, sharing very similar dental elements with those animals.
Specimens vary greatly in size, with measured lengths of 94, 24, and 22 millimeters, and possessed dorsal fin spines similar to those seen in Hetercanthus and Phlyctaenacanthus.
The species exhibits sexual dimorphism in the pelvic region, with males having claspers and females having large scale-like pelvic fins.
Fossil evidence suggests Ptyctodus likely fed on shellfish by crushing them with its specialized teeth.
The genus Ptyctodus was originally described by Pander in 1858.
Ptyctodus bradyi was discovered in 1942 by Hussakof on Mt. Elden in Arizona based on two tooth plates.
Ptyctodus lived as a nektonic carnivore in carbonate, lagoonal, and shallow subtidal environments.
It appears to have been an agile swimmer capable of escaping predators like arthrodires.
The genus includes the species P. bradyi, P. calceolus, P. compressus, P. ferox, P. molaris, and P. panderi, and is classified within the family Ptyctodontidae.
Ptyctodus lived during the late Devonian period, specifically from the Eifelian to the Famennian stages, between 393.47 and 358.86 million years ago.
Fossils of this fish have been found in Russia, Michigan, and Arizona, United States.
